stops.note: seize the day, from carpere (to pick, seize) and dies (day), first used by the poet Horace
from Horace's Odes (23 BC): 'carpe diem, quam minimum credula postero', seize the day, trust little in tomorrow
stops.meaning: an exhortation to enjoy and make the most of the present moment

current_meaning: an exhortation to make the most of the present moment
